title: Hardcoded Subclass Defaults in Traits
pattern: Providing default trait method implementations that are coupled to a specific implementer's requirements, forcing other implementers to override them or carry incorrect attributes.
why_bad: It violates the Liskov Substitution Principle. The default behavior is concrete and specific, not abstract. A mountain bike implementer is forced to carry or override `tape_color`, making the hierarchy untrustworthy.
detection: A trait method providing a default body that returns values or config details specific to only a subset of known implementers.
counterexample: Truly universal defaults (like empty lists or standard mathematical constants) that are invariant across all possible implementers.
fix: Do not provide a default implementation; force each implementer to define its own behavior, or separate the trait into cohesive sub-categories.
source: Sandi Metz, *Practical Object-Oriented Design* (2019), Chapter 7 ("Sharing Role Behavior... All code in an abstract superclass should apply to every class").
